title: Understanding Just-In-Time (JIT) Provisioning
content:
Just-In-Time (JIT) provisioning automatically creates a CloudDash user account the first time a team member logs in via Single Sign-On (SAML SSO). This eliminates the need for CloudDash administrators to manually invite users to the workspace.

## How JIT Works

1. A user clicks the CloudDash app icon in their corporate identity portal (e.g., Okta dashboard).
2. The IdP sends a SAML assertion to CloudDash containing the user's email, first name, and last name.
3. CloudDash checks if an account exists for that email address.
4. If no account exists, CloudDash automatically creates one on the fly, adds the user to your workspace, and logs them in.

## Enabling JIT Provisioning

1. Log in to CloudDash as an Admin.
2. Navigate to **Settings → Security & SSO**.
3. Scroll down to the **User Provisioning** section.
4. Toggle **Allow Just-In-Time (JIT) Provisioning** to ON.
5. Select the **Default Role** for newly provisioned users (Viewer or Editor). We strongly recommend setting this to 'Viewer' for security reasons.

## Attribute Requirements

For JIT to function, your IdP must send the user's name in the SAML assertion. If the `firstName` or `lastName` attributes are missing, the JIT process will fail and the user will see an error. Ensure your SAML attribute mappings are configured correctly (see kb-017).

## Seat Limits and JIT

If your CloudDash plan has a seat limit (e.g., 25 users on the Pro plan), JIT provisioning will fail if that limit has been reached. 

When user 26 attempts to log in, they will receive a message stating "Workspace seat limit reached. Contact your administrator." You must upgrade your plan or remove inactive users to allow new JIT logins.

## Deprovisioning (Offboarding)

JIT handles *creating* accounts, but SAML does not automatically *delete* accounts when a user leaves your company. 

If an employee departs, they will lose the ability to log in to CloudDash via SSO because their corporate account is disabled. However, their CloudDash user record will still consume a seat in your workspace. 

To free up the seat, a CloudDash Admin must manually remove the departed user via **Settings → Team & Permissions**. (Automated deprovisioning via SCIM is available exclusively on Enterprise plans).
